headline: Local Political Aspirant Promises To Not Only Become Prime Minister But Also Personally Fix Every Broken Streetlight In The Hemisphere
body:
A local independent candidate running for the upcoming legislative assembly has expanded his manifesto to include a promise to serve as Prime Minister, the next U.S. President, and the primary maintenance supervisor for the city’s flickering streetlights. The candidate, who filed his nomination papers yesterday via a carrier pigeon, told reporters that the scope of his governance is not limited by borders, geography, or the physical realities of city maintenance schedules.

“It’s about vision,” explained the candidate, while standing on a makeshift stage made of crates. “If I can manage a coalition government in Delhi, why wouldn't I be qualified to handle the nuances of the Electoral College in the United States? And frankly, the streetlights outside my house have been buzzing for three weeks, so I have already committed to personally replacing the bulbs myself once my international term begins.”

Political analysts are divided on whether the candidate’s expansion into municipal lighting repair is a bold campaign strategy or a logistical oversight. However, local residents seem cautiously optimistic about the dual-approach. “I don’t know much about his foreign policy regarding trade tariffs, but if he actually shows up with a ladder and a new bulb on Tuesday, he’s got my vote,” said a shopkeeper from the candidate’s constituency.

The candidate concluded his press conference by announcing that he will also be available for consultations on marital disputes and lunar exploration projects, provided they don't conflict with his lunch hour.
caption: Does your candidate also promise to handle your household chores? Let us know in the comments. #Elections #Manifesto #Politics #Infrastructure (satire)
igHook: Would you vote for someone if they promised to fix your neighborhood streetlights while running the country?
imagePrompt: A person stands on a makeshift wooden platform at a dusty roadside in an Indian neighborhood, addressing a small, curious group of passersby, with tangled overhead electrical wires visible in the background.
